# Brief 10: ESG assessment

Audience: Granite Mining board sustainability committee.
Decision: adopt a 2030 emissions pathway and fund $310M of abatement levers.
Format: 9 slides, density balanced. Start with a cover and end with next steps.
Data: data.csv holds emissions and safety data used on slides 3 and 5.

## Facts

F1: Scope 1 and 2 emissions (ktCO2e): 2023 842, 2024 801, 2025 763.
F2: The 2030 target is a 42% cut from the 2023 base, which is 488 ktCO2e.
F3: At the current pace of 4.8% a year, 2030 emissions would be about 597 ktCO2e, a gap of 109 ktCO2e.
F4: Abatement needed from 2025 to 2030: 275 ktCO2e. Levers: renewable power contracts 120, electrification of haul trucks 85, energy efficiency 45, fuel switching 25.
F5: Total abatement cost is $310M over five years: renewables 60, electrification 170, efficiency 50, fuel switching 30.
F6: Total recordable injury rate: Granite 1.9, peers 1.2 per million hours worked.
F7: Women hold 19% of leadership roles against a peer average of 27%.
F8: 62% of directors are independent; the governance code target is 66%.
F9: Water intensity fell 6% in 2025 to 1.9 cubic metres per tonne of ore.
F10: Two of three rating agencies give Granite a below-median rating; peers' median score is 62 and Granite scores 54.
F11: Scorecard status: environment amber, social red, governance amber.
F12: Peer injury rates per million hours: Peer A 0.9, Peer B 1.1, Peer C 1.3, Peer D 1.5; median 1.2.
